00.summary: Foreword items are listed but not counted in either figure, because the chapters cover the same ground. Of the four original Foreword objectives, two are in effect: DEI and gender-term removal (EO 14151, EO 14168 and EO 14173 of January 2025, plus later agency rules) and international withdrawals (EO 14155, EO 14199 and a 2026-01-07 memorandum covering 66 organizations). The free-speech objective is underway under EO 14149 and FTC actions. For the pornography objective, two introduced bills (S. 1671, H.R. 3297) are the closest step, with no committee action found, and court challenges to the DEI orders remain pending.

01.summary: One of four objectives is in effect: since 2025-02-25 the White House, not the White House Correspondents' Association, selects the press pool. Litigation continues: the Associated Press appeal was argued 2025-11-24 with no decision found, and on 2026-10-13 a district court preliminary injunction barred enforcement of the ban on three outlets while their case proceeds. Three objectives are underway: policy-council roles set by executive orders, Presidential Personnel Office clearance of Schedule C and Schedule G appointments, and a reported new White House Counsel contacts policy.

02.summary: Six of eight objectives are in effect. They rest on OMB's apportionment delegation (effective 2025-02-11), EO 14215 on OIRA review of independent agencies, CEQ's removal of its NEPA regulations (final rule effective 2026-01-08), EO 14168, EO 14148 and EO 14192 on regulatory review, and EO 14154 on social cost of carbon. NSC reorganization under NSPM-1 and a proposed amendment to the Fifth National Climate Assessment (noticed 2026-08-25) are underway, no life and family coordinator was found, and impoundment litigation continues.

03.summary: Five of nine objectives are in effect: Schedule Policy/Career (EO 14171 and EO 14410; OPM rule effective 2026-03-09), limits on union bargaining (EO 14251, EO 14343), merit hiring (EO 14170), workforce controls (EO 14210; OPM reduction-in-force rule effective 2026-09-02) and Schedule G (EO 14317). Appraisal and removal changes are underway, with OPM's probationary appeals rule effective 2026-09-02 and an MSPB penalty-review rule effective 2026-10-05, while pay and retirement legislation was not enacted. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB is classed as diverged, because OPM rules moved several appeal categories to OPM. Lawsuits over several actions are pending.

04.summary: Three of eleven objectives are in effect: EO 14183 on transgender service (the certiorari petition in United States v. Talbott, No. 26-272, is pending), EO 14184 on reinstating members discharged over the COVID-19 vaccine (about 230 returned by July 2026, against roughly 8,700 eligible) and EO 14185 on DEI offices. Seven are underway, including acquisition reform (EO 14265), Golden Dome (EO 14186) and a general-officer cut announced 2026-09-30; the fleet stood at 291 ships against a 355 goal, and one officer still leads both NSA and Cyber Command.

05.summary: Five of twelve objectives are in effect: nationwide expedited removal (in effect since 2026-07-17, rehearing petition pending), detention and ICE funding (P.L. 119-21, P.L. 119-98), ended parole and TPS programs, 287(g) growth (2,510 agreements by 2026-09-15) and a final public charge rule (effective 2026-09-18, challenged in S.D.N.Y.). Five are underway, including wall funding and border asylum limits (a certiorari petition in RAICES v. Noem is pending), while replacing DHS and shifting disaster costs to states remain at the proposal stage.

06.summary: Eleven of nineteen tracked recommendations are classed as in effect, including all seven key objectives, resting on EO 14163 (refugee entry suspended), EO 14155 and EO 14199 with a 2026-01-07 withdrawal memorandum covering 66 organizations, the State reorganization announced 2025-04-22, entry Proclamations 10949 and 10998, the EO 14169 aid pause, trade arrangements with the EU and the UK, and the return to the Geneva Consensus Declaration. Courts vacated a 75-country immigrant visa pause on 2026-08-21 and, temporarily, a diversity visa pause on 2026-08-28. Seven are underway, including cartel terrorist designations and icebreaker funding; no action was found on revoking Circular 175 authorities, and Somaliland is not recognized.

07.summary: One of nineteen tracked recommendations is in effect: ODNI was restructured from 2025-08-20 (ODNI 2.0) with staff reductions; clearance revocations under EO 14152, leak policy changes and CIA workforce changes are underway. FISA Title VII, including Section 702, lapsed on 2026-06-12 after House votes failed, and collection was reported to continue under existing certifications. Classification reform and a bar on monitoring domestic disinformation remain at the proposal stage, and no action on EO 14086 was found. Of the twelve recommendations added in the fuller reading, none is in effect: five are partly underway (clearance reform, intelligence support for export control and investment review, the reported move of President's Daily Brief production to ODNI, post-quantum orders EO 14412 and EO 14413 of 2026-06-22, and commercial space integration under EO 14369), four are at the proposal stage, and no public action was found on a 60-day covert action review, a 48-hour cyber threat sharing rule or the composition rule for the National Intelligence Council.

08.summary: Two of six tracked recommendations are in effect: the Rescissions Act of 2025 (P.L. 119-28, signed 2025-07-24) cancelled about $1.1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and acting leadership was installed at USAGM, although a 2026-03-07 court ruling voided one official's acting-CEO actions. Two are underway: EO 14238 (2025-03-14) directed USAGM reduced to its statutory minimum while Congress enacted about $652.7 million for FY2026. The NCE-status objective remains a proposal, and no journalist safety measures were found.

09.summary: Seven of twenty tracked recommendations are in effect, among them foreign assistance placed under State with USAID wound down by 2025-07-01, aid reductions (P.L. 119-28), rules on gender, equity and abortion terms (effective 2026-02-26), an AGOA extension, the end of climate finance under EO 14162 and appointee review of awards under EO 14332. Ten are underway or proposed, including humanitarian aid, global health compacts, regional aid resets and branding. One is classed as diverged (the WHO withdrawal), and no action was found on section 653(a) reporting or on the USAID staffing plan, which the agency wind-down made moot.

10.summary: Two of sixteen tracked recommendations are in effect: SNAP changes in P.L. 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) and the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines. Four are underway, including forest management, where the Forest Service finalized a shorter project objection process on 2026-10-13 (effective 2026-11-12), the end of climate-smart commodity grants on 2025-04-14, rejection of the UN 2030 Agenda and biotechnology review changes; four rest on introduced bills or early steps. Three are classed as diverged, as P.L. 119-21 raised ARC/PLC reference prices and added trade promotion funding, and CRP signups continued. No action was found on moving nutrition programs to HHS, marketing orders or the Community Eligibility Provision.

11.summary: Six of twenty-two tracked recommendations are in effect: removal of the 2024 Title IX rule, borrowing caps and a new repayment plan, removal of disparate-impact provisions from Title VI rules, charter grants run without the 2022 requirements, a revised Civil Rights Data Collection and USDA's rescission of its school meals Title IX policy. Nine are underway, including program moves to other agencies and Section 117 enforcement under EO 14282. Five rest on proposals or bills, the cap on research indirect costs is classed as diverged because Congress re-enacted the contrary bar after courts blocked the executive caps, and no move to end negotiated rulemaking was found.

12.summary: Of the 21 tracked Department of Energy and related commission recommendations, 4 are in effect, including LNG export approvals, the end of DOE equity programs, the refusal of climate reparations and, after a second review, the nuclear modernization funding with two plutonium pit sites and a sea-launched cruise missile. Twelve are underway, among them grid equipment security, cleanup and lab refocusing. Four have diverged, covering the Loan Programs Office, Yucca Mountain, FERC's transmission rule and reactor demonstrations (DOE awarded small modular reactor projects on 2025-12-02), none is blocked, and no action was found for ending the Clean Energy Corps.

13.summary: Of 21 tracked EPA recommendations, 6 are in effect (implemented or completed), including the restored 2020 major-source reclassification rule and relaxed HFC technology transition limits. Another 13 are underway (in progress or proposed), such as regional haze, Good Neighbor, truck NOx, Risk Management Program and TSCA procedure rulemakings. One, the PFAS hazardous substance designation, is recorded as diverged, none is blocked, and no action was found on a stand-alone American Indian Office.

14.summary: Of the 24 tracked recommendations in the health and human services chapter, 8 are in effect, including fetal tissue research limits, conscience enforcement, EMTALA guidance rescission, HSA rules confirmed by IRS guidance, CDC gender identity data, the inpatient-only list phase-out and, from 2026-10-13, the CMS rule barring Medicaid and CHIP payment for pediatric gender transition procedures, challenged by a 22-state suit and a New Hampshire families' suit with no injunction found. Ten are underway, three are blocked and three have diverged. FDA's mifepristone review report is due by March 2027.

15.summary: Of 15 tracked HUD recommendations, five are in effect, including the AFFH repeal, the end of PAVE appraisal policies, climate rollbacks, guidance withdrawals and reversals of prior diversity actions. Seven are underway, among them the noncitizen and work requirement proposals, Housing First changes, zoning and public housing provisions in a 2026 housing law, and budget-request devolution. None is blocked or diverged, and three show no action found: CFIUS membership, PD&R grant suspension and term-based FHA premiums.

16.summary: Of the 20 tracked Interior recommendations in this chapter, 8 are in effect (implemented), including oil and gas leasing, the 30 by 30 rescission, the Migratory Bird Treaty Act opinion, the Dalton corridor land order and congressional disapproval of recent BLM plans. Eleven are underway (7 in progress, 4 proposed), such as coal leasing, Endangered Species Act rules, the Boundary Waters and Chaco withdrawals and BLM headquarters, none are blocked or diverged, and 1, the BLM law enforcement chain of command, has no action found.

17.summary: Three of eighteen tracked recommendations are in effect: DOJ litigation aligned with the President's agenda (memo of 2025-02-05, EO 14215, Trump v. Slaughter of 2026-06-29), Civil Rights Division findings on race-conscious admissions, and the consent decree and FACE Act review. Twelve are underway, including death penalty authorizations, cartel prosecutions under a 2025-02-05 memo, the Weaponization Working Group review, EO 14149 limits on speech policing and border support under EO 14167. No action was found on Comstock Act enforcement, reassigning 18 U.S.C. 241 election cases or restarting the China Initiative.

18.summary: Three of twenty-two tracked recommendations are in effect: EO 11246 revoked by EO 14173 with a rescission rule effective 2026-10-26, the NLRB and EEOC general counsels replaced in January 2025, and the overtime threshold back near the first-term level. Seven are underway, including the Wagner-Peyser staffing rule effective 2026-10-19. Eight rest on proposals or bills, two show no action, project labor agreement deviations are blocked by a 2025-05-16 injunction, and the H-2A and H-2B cap is diverged; a 2026-08-26 ruling left the 2025 H-2A wage rule in place on remand.

19.summary: Three of fourteen tracked recommendations are in effect: NHTSA's fuel economy rule (published 2026-09-30) with resolutions on California waivers, and DOT rules restoring the 2019 rule on rules (effective 2026-05-27) and airline enforcement hearings (effective 2026-07-31). Five are underway, including air traffic control funding in P.L. 119-21, drone and eVTOL programs under EO 14307 and repeal of the FHWA carbon target rule. Four rest on proposals or bills, including Jones Act repeal bills of 2025-06-12; ending Essential Air Service is blocked after Congress funded it for FY2026, and no proposal to move MARAD was found.

20.summary: Two of twelve tracked recommendations are in effect: a VA rule restoring the exclusion of abortion services (effective 2026-01-30, under a Federal Circuit petition for review filed in May 2026) with a March 2025 rescission of the gender dysphoria directive, and the end of most telework announced 2025-02-03. Three are underway: claims processing, the Oracle health record rollout and scheduling changes. Three rest on proposals, including H.R. 740. Two are blocked: the rating schedule revision and the 2025-08-06 termination of union contracts, where a court restored the largest agreement.

21.summary: Three of fifteen tracked recommendations are in effect: NTIA's BEAD restructuring of 2025-06-06, revocation of the 30 by 30 order by EO 14148 and EO 14154, and the transfer of Baldrige operations to private partners announced 2025-12-11. Six are underway, including NOAA staffing cuts, a proposed census rule, export control rules, USPTO patent eligibility memoranda of December 2025 and marine monuments opened to fishing under EO 14276. Two are blocked, as Congress funded EDA, MBDA and MEP in P.L. 119-74; the TikTok divestiture is classed as diverged, and no action was found on consolidating trade promotion offices or restricting personal data exports.

22.summary: Two of eighteen tracked recommendations are in effect: the Corporate Transparency Act exemption for domestic companies (effective 2026-08-14) and withdrawal from the Paris Agreement (effective 2026-01-27) and the UN climate convention (notice recorded 2026-02-27). Seven are underway, including the IRA credit phase-out and estate tax changes in P.L. 119-21, the end of climate finance under EO 14162 and FSOC climate committees ended 2025-09-10. Four rest on bills or proposals, among them Universal Savings Account bills of May 2025. P.L. 119-21 kept seven individual rates and the BEAT and net investment income taxes, classed as diverged; no action was found on USTDA, a 50-year bond or merging bank regulators.

23.summary: The chapter presents two opposing positions. Reauthorizing the Export-Import Bank is underway: it operates with a three-member Board (President and Chair confirmed 2025-09-18), approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, and has a charter running to 2026-12-31, with S. 3772 and a House draft pending and no markup reported. Abolishing the Bank is classed as diverged, since no step toward abolition was found and the FY2027 request raises EXIM's program budget to $200 million.

24.summary: One of seven tracked recommendations is in effect: the bar on a central bank digital currency (executive order of 2025-01-23 and P.L. 119-101). Two are underway: H.R. 5396 on removing the employment goal, reported by committee 2026-06-24, and Fed regulation changes including withdrawal of climate principles. Shrinking the balance sheet is classed as diverged after reserve management purchases began 2025-12-11. No action was found on limiting last-resort lending, a commission on the Fed's mission, or a statutory monetary rule; the FOMC's framework statement of 2025-08-22 keeps a 2 percent goal.

25.summary: Two of thirteen tracked recommendations are in effect: the COVID-era loan fraud cleanup (870,000 suspensions announced 2026-09-14) and the end of SBA's voter registration role after EO 14148 revoked the 2021 voting order. Nine are underway, including SBIC changes in P.L. 119-92 (2026-05-19), the 2025-05-19 lender moratorium, the end of SBA diversity programs, H.R. 3174 on manufacturer loans (passed the House 2025-12-01), SBREFA bills and a FY2027 request cutting SBA 74.7 percent. No action was found on ending direct lending or a medium-sized business class.

26.summary: One of eighteen tracked recommendations is in effect: the end of de minimis treatment (EO 14256, EO 14324). Eight are underway, including Section 232 actions on chips and pharmaceuticals, 100 percent expensing in P.L. 119-21, the Section 805 defense procurement ban, sunsets under EO 14270 and a March 2026 USTR paper on WTO special treatment. Reciprocal tariff authority is blocked after Learning Resources v. Trump (2026-02-20); decoupling, tariff repeal, WTO dispute settlement and firm-level targeting are classed as diverged; no action was found on a COVID commission, trade adjustment assistance, counterfeit enforcement or a border adjustment tax.

27.summary: One of sixteen tracked recommendations is in effect: the SEC's 2025-03-14 rule ending the Enforcement Director's delegated authority to open formal investigations. Ten are underway, including the climate rule rescission proposal of 2026-05-29, capital formation proposals, the joint crypto interpretation of 2026-03-23, SEC regional restructuring, CFTC staff relief on cross-border swap definitions (2025-12-09) and bills on conflict minerals and broker-dealer audits. Abolishing the CFPB and the PCAOB and FINRA are blocked, and no action was found on ending administrative proceedings, a two-year investigation limit or CFTC governance amendments.

28.summary: None of six objectives is in effect. Four are underway: FCC Covered List additions of foreign-produced drones (2025-12-22), spectrum auctions required by P.L. 119-21 (Auction 115 proposed for 2027-04-27), satellite and wireline permitting actions, and an order repealing the 39 percent national television ownership cap (voted 2026-08-06, not yet published). The TikTok app was not banned (a U.S. joint venture closed 2026-01-22), platform contributions to the Universal Service Fund are proposed in two bills with no committee action, and no FCC action on Section 230 was found.

29.summary: None of three objectives is in effect. The coordination objective is underway through a court ruling: on 2026-06-30 the Supreme Court held in NRSC v. FEC, 6 to 3, that limits on party coordinated expenditures violate the First Amendment, and no statute raising contribution limits was found. The FEC has lacked a quorum since 2025-05-01, with two nominees named 2026-02-11 unconfirmed, and no directive limiting DOJ prosecution of FECA violations or having DOJ defend the FEC was found.

30.summary: One of four objectives is complete: Trump v. Slaughter (decided 2026-06-29, 6 to 3) held FTC commissioners removable at will and overruled Humphrey's Executor, after the President removed two commissioners on 2025-03-18. Three are underway through individual actions: consent orders barring advertising agencies from coordinating on political or ideological viewpoints, enforcement of the amended COPPA Rule with an AI chatbot inquiry, and non-price harm analysis in merger orders. No FTC task force on ESG or DEI collusion was found.

limits: The headline counts every recommendation tracked so far, 457 today, not every recommendation in the roughly 900-page document. The record began as key objectives from all 30 chapters and is being extended chapter by chapter by reading each chapter in full, so chapters read in full contribute more recommendations than the rest and the figure will move as more are added. Recommendations added in the fuller reading have had one independent review and no red-team pass yet. Foreword items are listed but not counted, because the chapters cover the same ground.
Research and review are done by AI models. Every claim links to its source so that a person can check it, and each objective carries a confidence rating. Errors are possible; corrections are welcome.

Research ran in five passes under a fixed web search budget: a first pass on 2026-10-07, a validation pass on the weakest and in-effect objectives, an in-depth pass that re-researched weak records and added objectives in every chapter, a targeted pass on 2026-10-08 on every objective still rated low confidence, and a primary-source pass the same day that located the deciding official document for records previously rated on secondary sources. Objectives rated medium or low confidence still rest on limited searching, and developments from mid-2026 onward are the most likely to be missing.
A status of "No action found" means the research found none. It is weaker evidence than a documented action, and the reviewer caps its confidence accordingly.
Objectives are not independent. One law, order, or court ruling can count toward several objectives, so the headline share is not a count of separate government actions.
Progress percentages come from a fixed rubric and the average is unweighted. Objectives differ greatly in importance, so the average is a rough gauge only.
Status describes alignment between actions and the document. Officials have said the administration does not follow the document, and many actions have other origins.
Estimated timeframes are inferences from the legal route each objective needs. They are not predictions from any official schedule.

significance.note: Recomputed on 2026-10-11 for the single headline set of 257 counted recommendations. The page computes the weighted share live from the scores on each record. Rater agreement figures are from the original scoring of 219 objectives; the bootstrap range has not been recomputed.

trackers.name: Project 2025 Tracker (project2025.observer)
trackers.note: a community tracker organized by agency with three statuses (completed, in progress, not started); it listed 321 objectives with 141 completed and 70 in progress when read on 2026-10-08. It runs advertising and donation links.

trackers.name: Center for Progressive Reform and Governing for Impact executive action tracker
trackers.note: an advocacy-organization tracker; it reported 283 of 532 domestic executive actions initiated or completed as of its February 2026 update.

update_note: The record is refreshed every Tuesday and Thursday morning (Pacific time). Each run searches official sources and the press for developments on every tracked objective, updates status and evidence, sends changed objectives to an independent review, and logs the changes under Changes. Daily runs are planned once the beta settles. Requests made under Requirements are picked up by the next run.
